column2: Coded from the abstract, official proceedings/publisher page and project page of each work (single coder). 'U' (undetermined) = not determinable from these sources; to be resolved by full-text reading.
none: no human data; outputs: human-made images/sketches without temporal order; process: human stroke sequences, trajectories or videos of making.
Yes if the authors explicitly motivate the design by human cognition, perception or motor control.
Yes if humans rate, prefer or classify generated outputs.

Yes if generated order, trajectory, kinematics or temporal progression are compared quantitatively with recorded human data. This includes aggregated temporal comparisons with human sequences (e.g. cumulative progression vs QuickDraw), which are weaker than exact matching of trajectories or stroke order; such cases are flagged in 'Basis / note'.
Yes if model behaviour is compared with the behaviour of a population of human participants (accuracy patterns, errors, variability, choices).
D, J, P and B are independent dimensions, not a scale. Human data used for training is recorded separately from human data used for validation.

Counts cover the 50 generative approaches of the final corpus (this sheet). Surveys, evaluation-methodology papers, datasets and cognitive studies without a generative model are listed in S2 but not coded. One candidate record was excluded (Pearce et al. 2023: game imitation, outside scope). S1 ID A20 corresponds to corpus ID H13.

Codes were first assigned from abstracts and official pages, then revised by full-text reading where available. Every code changed after full-text reading carries its evidence (study size, section or source) in the 'Basis / note' column.
